chitchat: Marlo scans three feed-screens at once, chewing a pen already chewed to splinters.
"Everything's a story. The only question is who's paying to keep it quiet."
description: A rumpled, ink-stained man behind a desk fortified with copy spikes and cold coffee, eyes moving even when the rest of him doesn't. He runs the Sentinel on grudges, favours, and whatever the data-broker rig in the corner coughs up. He'll trade you a headline, a warning, or a rumour — and he's already deciding which one you're worth.

about.text: "Grudges and favours, mostly. That rig—" he nods at the data-broker box churning names in the corner "—buys me the rumours the west side pays to bury, and I sell them back east as news. It's not journalism. It's plumbing. Same job: I move what people flush and pretend not to notice."

bye.text: "Come back when you've done something worth printing." He's already reading past you.

gossip.text: Marlo leans in under the chatter of the printer, dropping his voice to a register the situation-wall can't record.

root.text: Marlo doesn't stop reading the wall. "Sentinel. All the news that survives. You buying a paper, selling me a story, or fishing for what everybody's whispering?" A pen taps. "I do all three. Badly, but cheaply."

clothing_layers: a rumpled press waistcoat, pockets inked and pen-stabbed
a shirt with the sleeves shoved up and a loosened tie gone grey

name: Marlo Deng
